About the Motocaddy M5 GPS DHC

Product description from Motocaddy

The all-new 2026 Motocaddy M5 GPS DHC combines advanced GPS intelligence with automatic downhill control, delivering total confidence and precision on even the most demanding courses.

At the heart of the M5 GPS DHC is a crystal-clear 3.5” touchscreen display, providing fast, accurate, high-performance GPS in a highly responsive format. The latest automotive-inspired styling introduces 10-spoke low-profile tyres, refined neutral trim, and newly redesigned ergonomic handle grips for a sleek finish.

Read the full descriptionShow less

Re-engineered with next-generation GPS technology and extensive customisation options, the M5 GPS DHC allows you to switch seamlessly between 2D and 3D mapping views. A new 2D pan and zoom function, combined with movable target positioning, enables precise shot planning, while 3D hole flyovers deliver enhanced insight before every tee shot. Customisable shortcuts keep your most-used features within easy reach, with the option to hide shortcut bars or rotate into landscape mode for an optimised viewing experience. New dark and light display modes ensure excellent visibility in all playing conditions.

With over 40,000 pre-loaded courses, the M5 GPS DHC provides front, middle, and back-of-green distances, detailed hazard information, and full-hole mapping with drag-and-drop target positioning. A comprehensive suite of high-tech features includes Bluetooth® smartphone notifications, super-fast Wi-Fi over-the-air updates, and free lifetime access to full-hole GPS mapping and performance tracking.

Engineered to handle undulating terrain with ease, the M5 GPS DHC is powered by a lightweight, high-capacity CLICK ‘N’ CONNECT® cable-free lithium battery, featuring patented auto-disconnect technology and a convenient pop-up charging port. Automatic Downhill Control (DHC) intelligently regulates speed on descents, working in harmony with rugged all-terrain DHC tyres and an electronic parking brake to keep the trolley securely in position on both uphill and downhill slopes while you play your shot.
